description.value: The study examined relationships between self-reported positive and negative affect and task-related fMRI activation during an emotional interference conflict task in women with PTSD and healthy controls.

spans.text: The current study sought to determine the relationship between self-reported dimensions of affect and activation in brain regions associated with emotion regulation in PTSD during a task of non-conscious emotional processing in interpersonal trauma survivors with PTSD and healthy controls.

description.value: Observational, between-group study of women with PTSD and healthy controls using a task-based fMRI assessment.

spans.text: The purpose of this study is to observe the relationship between self-reported dimensions of affect and brain activation during the emotionally evocative conditions of the conflict task (e.g., AF and IF) and how this relationship differs between individuals with PTSD and healthy controls.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to attend to either the horizontal or vertical pair and indicate whether the stimuli were the same or different while ignoring the other pair.

spans.text: Subjects must then indicate whether these stimuli are the same or different by pressing corresponding buttons with the right hand while ignoring the other stimulus pair.
